Sound Garden

The Pipe Rack

A wall of tuned bronze pipes. Run your hand across them and they play as you cross — low on the left, high on the right. Rest on one and it hums its own short voice; click and it opens the room. Every chord is consonant by construction.

the air give the rack its air, then sweep the pipes
The lower shelf

Four benches that take a sound apart

The garden mostly plays; these four reason. Each proves one law of how a vibration is built, bounded, or shared — the bass pipes of the rack, tuned an octave down. Sweep across them and you hear the wall run down to the low brass.

▶ strum The Butterfly the FFT laid on a wheel: any sound falls apart into its pure tones, one bin to a spoke. ▶ strum The Singing Glass sweep a pure tone past a wine glass and hear it wake only at its own note; resonance, made audible. ▶ strum The Sampling Theorem Nyquist's line: the exact rate below which a captured tone lies about its pitch. ▶ strum The Trading Bench two coupled pendulums pour one swing back and forth, beat for beat (kin of The Beating Bench).

The garden's rigorous voices: ↔ The Butterfly's Voice proves a note's pitch IS its FFT bin · ↔ The Comma winds twelve true fifths and HEARS them miss the octave · ↔ Out of Tune turns a brass orrery dial and HEARS the solar-system chord land out of tune · ↔ The Monochord plucks one string and SEES + HEARS its overtones are an exactly even ladder (fₙ/f₁=n) · ↔ The Beating Bench DRAG one tone over a drone and HEAR the throb die to silence at each just ratio · ↔ The Quorum TWIST one knob and HEAR sixteen ticking clocks snap from a hailstorm into a single heartbeat · ↔ The Overtone Rack DRAG twelve brass faders and HEAR a timbre take shape — then pull the fundamental and the pitch survives · ↔ The Plucked Reed PLUCK a brass reed and HEAR a burst of hiss self-organize into a pitched string — then drag DECAY to zero and it falls back into the raw noise it was made of · ↔ The Stopped Pipe CAP one end of the Plucked Reed's echo loop — one sign flip — and HEAR the pipe drop a clean octave while its even voices wink out: the odd-only clarinet bore (the boundary picks the overtones the Overtone Rack picks by hand) · ↔ The Vowel Throat DRAG a glowing dot through vowel-space and HEAR a toneless glottal buzz become "ah…ee…oo" — the throat CARVES the voice; nothing is added (the Overtone Rack's subtractive mirror) · ↔ The Endless Staircase TURN a brass dial and HEAR a chord climb forever yet land exactly home every octave — then flip the envelope flat and hear it climb out and never return · ↔ The Tartini Bench TUNE two brass tone-wheels through a slightly-bent horn and HEAR a third pitch nobody played bloom at f₂−f₁ — then flip the horn to LINEAR and it vanishes · ↔ The Squeal Bench DRAG a bow across a taut fibre and feel one stick-slip motion morph — fast & light it SINGS a violin sawtooth, slow & hard it CREAKS like a door, stiff & barely-moving it QUAKES in countable thuds — with NO mode button; a violin, a hinge, and an earthquake are one law · ↔ The Sidebands PUSH the depth β and HEAR one carrier sprout a whole comb of sidebands at fc±n·fm, each rung |Jₙ(β)| tall — then at β≈2.4048 the carrier itself goes dark · ↔ The Comb DRAG one brass delay and SEE a comb of notches slide across the spectrum while you HEAR the jet-plane flange whoosh — the first tooth at 1/(2τ), spaced 1/τ; the time-domain mirror of The Sidebands (a delay NOTCHES energy OUT of a spectrum where FM SPREADS energy INTO one), then collapse the delay and the teeth vanish · ↔ The Jug FILL a brass jug and BLOW across its mouth: it HUMS one low note with NO overtone ladder — the air-plug in the neck is a MASS bobbing on the cavity's air SPRING. Halve the water-space and the hum jumps a tritone (×√2); quadruple the neck and it drops an octave — the lumped foil to The Stopped Pipe's distributed odd-harmonic series · ↔ Hearing the Shape STRIKE two drumheads that are plainly not the same shape and hear them answer with the SAME fourteen notes, agreeing to fifteen digits — Kac’s 1966 question, answered no. Nothing was cited: the room cuts seven half-squares, enumerates all 318 shapes you can glue them into, solves the Laplacian on every one and compares 50,403 pairs in half a second, and exactly one pair comes back identical. Swap in the best liar of the other 316 — same area, same perimeter, same eight corners — and its first six notes are inside a cent and a third before its seventh gives it away. Then HOLD a mode: same frequency, different nodal picture (the struck-MEMBRANE foil to The Singing Plate’s driven disc) · ↔ The Wind Chimes STAND UNDER a chime hung in three dimensions and RAISE the wind: six tubes cut so the METAL decides the note (a free-free beam, partials 1 : 2.756 : 5.404 …, so it can be neither bell nor string), swinging on their own cords in air that gusts and veers. TAP one anywhere along its length and hear where you hit; DRAG the cord along it and hear twelve seconds of ring fall to two — then MEASURE IT, and watch the page fit T60 to 33 strikes of its own audio and land on 0.2242, the point where mode 1 stands still (the struck-TUBE foil to The Carillon's bells) · ↔ The Answering Room STAND INSIDE the lattice of mirror-rooms a clap makes — every echo in a box is a straight line from a mirror image of the source, so the whole infinite family of them is a tiling you can walk around; hand four hundred thousand of those mirrors to a real convolver and HEAR the room they describe, then watch its decay refuse the straight line both textbook formulas assume · ↔ The Belfry GO UP THE LADDER into the bell chamber while a band is ringing underneath you — six bells turning full circle on their wheels, each one TWO coupled pendulums (the bell about its gudgeons, the clapper about its own pivot inside it), integrated as you watch, sounding at the instant the clapper actually arrives. A bell's balance is not upright: the clapper lying on the trailing soundbow holds it 0.70° over, and that offset is the POLE of the timing law, so the fall time is a - b ln(ε - ε*) to six figures and the fitted slope is the linearised growth rate to 0.07%. Which is why the ringer is ONE STROKE BEHIND: LEAN ON A ROPE and the blow the bell is already falling towards does not move, and the next one moves by a third of a second. CUT A BELL OPEN and watch the clapper for a whole revolution · ↔ The Spiral Ear THE ONE PIECE IN THIS ROOM THAT LISTENS instead of sounding: thirty-five millimetres of membrane wound two and a half times round a cone, with water on both faces, solved live as you play. DRAG a tone along the rail and the travelling wave crawls to the ONE place that answers it — and the peak is not where you would put it, standing 1.60 mm basal of the place whose resonance matches, at every frequency. PULL THE SHELL STRAIGHT and lay a ruler on it: the octave is 3.5120 mm wide wherever you put it. Past its own place a tone dies at √(2ρ/HM) = 65.66 dB/mm, a closed form with NO FREQUENCY IN IT — which is the whole reason a loud low note drowns a quiet high one and never the reverse. TAKE THE WATER AWAY and all of it goes: symmetric tuning, no travelling wave, the peak exactly at resonance. Then TAP it, and watch one instant come out the other end as a sixty-millisecond glide · ↔ The Tone Mill CRANK a toothed brass siren disc and WATCH the rate become the pitch — f = N·Ω/2π — the same just lattice the monochord plucks, here a spun rate you freeze with a strobe.
